blocks.text: Privileged Remote Access (PRA) allows you to provide temporary remote access to specific applications with Private Access (ZPA). PRA allows contractors and third-party users access to specific applications. You must first set up privileged portals and privileged consoles.
PRA applications provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Quickly identify which application segments are enabled for PRA.
See which ports and protocols have been configured for PRA.
Apply filters to change the view of PRA-enabled application segments.

blocks.text: On the Privileged Applications page (Zero Trust Browser > Privileged Remote Access > Privileged Applications), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Expand all the rows in the table to see more information about each application.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.
View a list of all applications that were specifically configured for PRA within an application segment. For each application, you can see:
Name: The name of the application. When expanded, the following information is displayed:
Segment Group: The segment group that the application segment is a member of.
Server Groups: The server groups that the application is hosted on.
Domain: The FQDN associated with the application.

Application Protocol: The protocol (VNC, RealVNC, SSH, or RDP) used for the application. To learn more about Windows and FIPS-enforced requirements for RDP, see Configuring Defined Application Segments.
Application Port: The port number used for the application.
